definition: a device that launches or hurls objects through the air with great force

collocations.example: The aircraft catapult hurled the jet off the carrier deck.
Soldiers used a medieval catapult to hurl heavy stones.

definition: a meeting of members of a political party to choose candidates or decide policy

collocations.example: The party caucus met to choose its new leader.
Delegates attended the caucus meeting before the final vote.

definition: relating to the sky or to objects in outer space

collocations.example: Astronomers study the movement of distant celestial bodies.
Sailors once relied on celestial navigation at sea.

definition: the state of not marrying or having sexual relations, often for religious reasons

collocations.example: The monk took a solemn vow of celibacy.
He chose a life of celibacy and quiet prayer.

definition: a large stringed musical instrument played with a bow, lower in tone than a violin

collocations.example: She learned to play the cello as a child.
The concert opened with a beautiful cello solo.

definition: strong, formal expression of disapproval or criticism

definition: a machine that spins rapidly to separate substances of different densities

He loaded the blood into a small centrifuge tube.

definition: a large decorative light fixture that hangs from the ceiling

Workers carefully hung a chandelier in the entrance hall.

definition: a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses, used in ancient times for war or racing

definition: the base frame of a vehicle, onto which the body and parts are fixed

Engineers strengthened the chassis frame for extra safety.

definition: not having sexual relations, or behaving in a pure and modest way

The poem describes a chaste and modest young heroine.

definition: a large country house or castle in France

definition: a person employed to drive someone's car

The hotel offers a chauffeur service for its guests.

definition: a chemical compound of chlorine with another element, such as a metal

definition: a serious infectious disease that causes severe diarrhoea and can be fatal

Poor sanitation caused the cholera epidemic to spread quickly.

definition: to give a name to a baby at a Christian baptism ceremony

collocations.example: The priest will christen the baby on Sunday.

definition: hard, shiny metal plating used to coat and decorate metal surfaces

definition: a sloping channel or tube down which things can slide or drop

The building has a rubbish chute on each floor.

definition: used before a date to mean approximately or around

definition: to find a way around a rule or problem in order to avoid it

definition: a strong fortress, usually on high ground, that protects or dominates a city

Soldiers defended the citadel overlooking the river.

definition: a juicy fruit such as an orange, lemon, or lime, or the tree that bears it

collocations.example: Oranges and lemons are popular citrus fruits.
They own a large citrus grove in Florida.

definition: a sea creature with a hard shell in two halves, eaten as food

collocations.example: We ordered a bowl of hot clam chowder.
They dug for clams along the sandy beach.

definition: done secretly, especially because it is not allowed

collocations.example: The spies held a clandestine meeting at midnight.
The group planned a clandestine operation abroad.

definition: a woodwind instrument played by blowing and covering holes with the fingers

collocations.example: She learned to play the clarinet in school.
The band needed a skilled bass clarinet player.

definition: a phrase or idea used so often that it is no longer original or interesting

collocations.example: Try to avoid that tired cliche in your essay.
The once-fresh phrase has now become a cliche.

definition: the customers of a shop, restaurant, or business considered as a group

collocations.example: The restaurant attracts a wealthy and exclusive clientele.
The small shop has built up a loyal clientele.

definition: a small wild plant with leaves in three parts and usually pink or white flowers

collocations.example: She searched the lawn for a four-leaf clover.
The cows grazed in a wide field of clover.

definition: a hard, silvery-gray metal, often used to produce a deep blue coloring

Engineers used a strong cobalt alloy for the parts.

definition: a poisonous snake that can spread the skin of its neck into a hood

A king cobra can grow remarkably long.

definition: to arrange laws or rules into a clear, organized system

definition: the mental process of gaining knowledge and understanding through thinking and the senses

collocations.example: Researchers study how human cognition develops in young children.
Memory plays a key role in social cognition.

definition: a sweet, brown, fizzy drink flavored with extract from the kola nut

collocations.example: He bought a cold can of cola.
She prefers diet cola to regular sweet soda.

definition: a picture made by sticking various materials or photographs onto a surface

collocations.example: The children created a colorful photo collage together.
She made a collage from old magazine clippings.

definition: property or assets promised to a lender in case a loan is not repaid

collocations.example: He used his house as collateral for the loan.
The bank required collateral for the large loan.

definition: to work together secretly in order to do something dishonest or illegal

collocations.example: The firms colluded to fix the market price.
He was accused of colluding with his rivals.

definition: extremely large in size or amount

collocations.example: The failed project was a colossal waste of money.
They spent a colossal amount on advertising.

definition: an informal word for a combination of things, such as a set meal

collocations.example: He ordered the chicken combo meal for lunch.
The dish is a tasty combo of two flavors.

definition: land or resources that belong to or are shared by a whole community

definition: sudden noisy activity or confusion, usually caused by excitement or trouble

collocations.example: The loud argument caused a commotion in the street.
A sudden commotion woke the sleeping hotel guests.

definition: a group of people who live together and share property and responsibilities

collocations.example: They decided to live in a rural commune.
Several young artists joined the commune in the hills.

definition: the state of being calm and in control of your feelings

collocations.example: She paused to regain her composure before speaking.
He managed to maintain his composure under great pressure.

definition: resulting from a strong urge that is difficult to control

collocations.example: He finally sought help for his compulsive gambling.
Compulsive behavior can be a sign of stress.

definition: planned and done together by several people in a determined way

definition: giving a lot of information clearly in few words

collocations.example: The report was clear, accurate, and concise.
She wrote a concise summary of the long meeting.

definition: happening at the same time as something else and connected with it

collocations.example: Rapid growth brought a concomitant increase in pollution.

definition: to do something you think is beneath your dignity, often in a superior way

collocations.example: She would not condescend to speak to us.
He rarely condescends to help the junior staff.

definition: to accept or allow behavior that is generally considered wrong

collocations.example: I do not condone violence of any kind.

definition: making a particular situation or result likely to happen

collocations.example: A quiet room is conducive to effective learning.
These conditions are conducive to steady economic growth.

definition: a sweet food such as a cake or candy, often elaborately made

collocations.example: The bakery sold a rich, sweet chocolate confection.

definition: present from the time a person is born

Doctors detected a congenital defect in the newborn infant.

definition: an evergreen tree that produces cones and has needle-like leaves

collocations.example: The steep hillside was covered with a conifer forest.
A tall conifer stood beside the wooden cabin.

definition: an opinion or conclusion based on incomplete information; a guess

collocations.example: His theory was based on pure conjecture.
The true cause remains a matter of conjecture.

definition: to make or declare something sacred in a religious ceremony

collocations.example: The bishop will consecrate the new church next month.
The priests consecrated the altar during the ceremony.

definition: important because of the likely effects or results

collocations.example: The committee discussed several highly consequential matters.
It was a very consequential decision for the firm.

definition: a speech sound made by partly or fully blocking the breath, like b, c, or d

definition: to become narrower or make something narrower or tighter

definition: showing great skill and perfection

collocations.example: He played the difficult part with consummate skill.
She is a consummate professional in her field.

definition: something that naturally follows or results from another thing

collocations.example: Higher sales were a corollary of better advertising.
Stress is a natural corollary of modern working life.

definition: the ceremony at which a king or queen is formally crowned

collocations.example: Thousands of people attended the king's coronation ceremony.
The royal coronation took place in the ancient cathedral.

definition: to provide evidence that supports or confirms a statement or finding

collocations.example: Two witnesses corroborated the victim's account.
New data corroborate the earlier research findings.

definition: the outer layer of an organ in the body, especially the brain

collocations.example: The cerebral cortex controls thought and memory.
The visual cortex processes what the eyes see.

definition: to accept, approve, or tolerate something

collocations.example: The committee refused to countenance his risky proposal.
She would not countenance the idea of leaving.

definition: to reduce or cancel the bad effect of something with an opposite action

collocations.example: These exercises counteract the harmful effects of stress.
Medicine was given to counteract the poison.

definition: made as an exact copy of something in order to deceive people

collocations.example: The police seized a pile of counterfeit money.
Customs officers found several boxes of counterfeit goods.

definition: a woman who holds the rank of count or earl, or is the wife of one

The dowager countess lived alone in the old castle.

definition: a person or company that delivers packages and documents quickly

collocations.example: The courier service delivers parcels within a few hours.
We sent the signed contract by courier yesterday.

definition: polite, respectful, and considerate towards other people

collocations.example: The hotel staff were friendly, polite, and courteous.
Customers really appreciate quick and courteous service.

definition: the period during which a couple build a romantic relationship before marriage

collocations.example: After a short courtship, the couple got married.

definition: a person you work with, especially someone at a similar level

collocations.example: She asked a coworker for help with the report.
A friendly coworker showed him around the new office.

definition: to burn a dead body to ashes, usually as part of a funeral

collocations.example: The grieving family chose to cremate the body.
He asked to be cremated after his death.

definition: the scientific study of crime and criminals

collocations.example: She decided to study criminology at university.
He holds a master's degree in criminology.

definition: to feel very embarrassed or uncomfortable about something

collocations.example: I cringe when I recall my awful speech.

definition: to speak in a rough, low voice, especially because of a sore throat

collocations.example: With a sore throat, she could only croak a greeting.
He croaked hoarsely into the telephone.

definition: a support held under the arm to help an injured person walk

collocations.example: He walked on crutches after breaking his leg.
The nurse handed him a pair of crutches.

definition: a small enclosed space or compartment within a larger room

collocations.example: She works all day in a small office cubicle.
He got changed in a cubicle beside the pool.

definition: an art style that shows objects as geometric shapes seen from many angles

collocations.example: The young painter was strongly influenced by cubism.
Analytic cubism broke everyday objects into geometric shapes.

definition: a gray bird known for its call and for laying eggs in other birds' nests

collocations.example: A cuckoo clock hung on the kitchen wall.
We heard the cuckoo's call across the quiet valley.

definition: to reduce the number of animals in a group by killing some of them

collocations.example: Officials decided to cull part of the deer herd.
Farmers were ordered to cull all infected animals.

definition: large, heavy, and difficult to use, carry, or manage

collocations.example: The hiker carried a heavy, cumbersome backpack all day.

definition: an official order requiring people to stay indoors after a particular time

collocations.example: The army imposed a nighttime curfew on the city.
The whole town was placed under curfew.

definition: a sweet yellow sauce or dessert made from milk, eggs, and sugar

collocations.example: She poured warm custard over the apple pie.
The dessert was a smooth, rich egg custard.

definition: a small wild flower with white petals and a yellow center

collocations.example: The children made a long chain of daisies.
A single daisy grew beside the garden path.

definition: to repair a hole in clothing by weaving stitches across it

collocations.example: She sat down to darn her son's socks.
He tried to darn the hole in his sweater.

definition: a situation in which no progress can be made because sides disagree

collocations.example: The lengthy negotiations have reached a complete deadlock.
A last-minute offer helped break the deadlock.

definition: to make a person or thing very weak

collocations.example: The long illness began to debilitate his body.
A poor diet can slowly debilitate a growing child.

definition: an amount of money taken out of a bank account

collocations.example: A debit of fifty dollars appeared on her statement.
We pay the monthly rent by direct debit.

definition: a state of low moral standards and an excessive love of pleasure

collocations.example: The empire slowly fell into moral decadence.

definition: the act of making someone believe something that is not true

collocations.example: He was accused of lies and deceit.
She grew tired of his life of deceit.

definition: to damage someone's good reputation by saying false things about them

collocations.example: The article was written to defame an honest man.
He sued the paper for trying to defame his reputation.

definition: to cut down and remove all the trees from an area

collocations.example: The spreading fires will permanently deforest the land.

definition: to make a dangerous or tense situation calmer and less harmful

collocations.example: Local police worked hard to defuse the racial tension.

definition: to lose or remove water from the body or a substance

collocations.example: Runners can dehydrate quickly in this intense heat.

definition: to search deeply and thoroughly for information

collocations.example: She began to delve into her family's history.
The reporter promised to delve deeper into the case.

definition: to make someone lose confidence, hope, or courage

collocations.example: A heavy defeat can demoralise the whole team.

definition: to remove a ruler or leader from a position of power

collocations.example: The rebels planned to depose the king.

definition: an important sports match between two teams from the same area or city

collocations.example: The two city teams meet in a local derby.

definition: (of a building or land) abandoned and in a very poor condition

collocations.example: Her body was found in a derelict warehouse.
